titulo_es: Comunicación profesional y habilidades para la vida
estandares: Me comunico en situaciones formales y laborales con el registro adecuado. Describo mis capacidades, limitaciones y proyectos con estructuras complejas.
competencias: Usar modales y modales perfectos en contexto profesional; enlazar ideas con conjunciones subordinantes; formular preguntas indirectas; hablar de oficios, talentos, fortalezas y entrevistas.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En parejas, los estudiantes preparan y representan una entrevista de trabajo: hoja de vida, carta de presentación, preguntas indirectas del entrevistador y respuestas sobre fortalezas y debilidades.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In pairs, students prepare and act out a job interview: a résumé, a cover letter, the interviewer's indirect questions and answers about strengths and weaknesses.

lecciones.content_es:
Graduar el mensaje

  • must / have to: obligación firme — Applicants must submit two references.
  • should / ought to: recomendación — You should tailor your résumé.
  • can / could: capacidad y petición — I can manage teams. / Could you send the details?
  • may / might: posibilidad y permiso formal — The position may involve travel.
  • would: cortesía e hipótesis — I would be glad to contribute.

Cortesía profesional

Cuanto más indirecto, más formal: Can you…? < Could you…? < Would you mind…? < I was wondering if you could…

Reglas fijas

Los modales no llevan -s, no llevan to (salvo ought to) y forman negativo y pregunta sin do.

Sustitutos

Cuando se necesita otro tiempo: be able to (can), have to (must), be allowed to (may).
lecciones.content_en:
Grading the message

  • must / have to: firm obligation — Applicants must submit two references.
  • should / ought to: recommendation — You should tailor your résumé.
  • can / could: ability and request — I can manage teams. / Could you send the details?
  • may / might: possibility and formal permission — The position may involve travel.
  • would: politeness and hypothesis — I would be glad to contribute.

Professional politeness

The more indirect, the more formal: Can you…? < Could you…? < Would you mind…? < I was wondering if you could…

Fixed rules

Modals take no -s, no to (except ought to) and form negatives and questions without do.

Substitutes

When another tense is needed: be able to (can), have to (must), be allowed to (may).

lecciones.content_es:
La fórmula

modal + have + participio, siempre igual: should have sent, could have been.

Qué expresa cada uno

  • should have: crítica o arrepentimiento — I should have prepared more examples.
  • shouldn't have: algo que no debió hacerse.
  • could have: posibilidad no aprovechada — You could have applied earlier.
  • would have: lo que habría pasado — I would have accepted, but the salary was too low.
  • must have: deducción casi segura — They must have received the email.
  • can't have: deducción negativa — She can't have forgotten the meeting.
  • might / may have: suposición — He might have misunderstood.

Errores

No existe would of ni should of: la forma es have. Y el verbo va en participio, no en pasado.
lecciones.content_en:
The formula

modal + have + participle, always the same: should have sent, could have been.

What each one expresses

  • should have: criticism or regret — I should have prepared more examples.
  • shouldn't have: something that should not have been done.
  • could have: an unused possibility — You could have applied earlier.
  • would have: what would have happened — I would have accepted, but the salary was too low.
  • must have: near-certain deduction — They must have received the email.
  • can't have: negative deduction — She can't have forgotten the meeting.
  • might / may have: a guess — He might have misunderstood.

Mistakes

There is no would of or should of: the form is have. And the verb goes in the participle, not the past.

lecciones.content_es:
Qué hacen

Unen una oración principal con una subordinada y establecen la relación entre ambas.

  • Tiempo: when, while, before, after, until, as soon as, once
  • Causa: because, since, as
  • Contraste: although, even though, though, whereas, while
  • Condición: if, unless, provided that, as long as, in case
  • Propósito: so that, in order that
  • Resultado: so … that, such … that

Puntuación

Si la subordinada va primero, se separa con coma: Although the salary was low, she accepted. Si va después, no lleva coma.

Detalles

  • while sirve para tiempo y para contraste: el contexto decide.
  • so that introduce propósito y suele llevar modal: so that we can finish on time.
  • so … that con adjetivo; such … that con sustantivo: so busy that… / such a busy week that…
lecciones.content_en:
What they do

They join a main clause with a subordinate one and set the relation between them.

  • Time: when, while, before, after, until, as soon as, once
  • Cause: because, since, as
  • Contrast: although, even though, though, whereas, while
  • Condition: if, unless, provided that, as long as, in case
  • Purpose: so that, in order that
  • Result: so … that, such … that

Punctuation

If the subordinate clause comes first, separate it with a comma: Although the salary was low, she accepted. If it comes second, no comma.

Details

  • while works for time and for contrast: the context decides.
  • so that introduces purpose and usually takes a modal: so that we can finish on time.
  • so … that with an adjective; such … that with a noun: so busy that… / such a busy week that…

lecciones.content_es:
Para qué sirven

Son más corteses y formales que la pregunta directa. Muy usadas en entrevistas y correos.

La transformación

Después de la fórmula introductoria, el orden es el de una afirmación: sin inversión y sin do/does/did.

  • Where is the office? → Could you tell me where the office is?
  • What time does it start? → Do you know what time it starts?
  • Did he apply? → I'd like to know if he applied.

Fórmulas introductorias

Could you tell me… · Do you know… · I was wondering… · I'd like to know… · Would you mind telling me…

Detalles

  • Con preguntas de sí o no se usa if o whether.
  • Si la fórmula es una pregunta (Do you know…?), la oración lleva signo de interrogación; si es una afirmación (I'd like to know…), lleva punto.
lecciones.content_en:
What they are for

They are more polite and formal than the direct question. Very common in interviews and emails.

The transformation

After the introductory formula, the word order is that of a statement: no inversion and no do/does/did.

  • Where is the office? → Could you tell me where the office is?
  • What time does it start? → Do you know what time it starts?
  • Did he apply? → I'd like to know if he applied.

Introductory formulas

Could you tell me… · Do you know… · I was wondering… · I'd like to know… · Would you mind telling me…

Details

  • With yes/no questions use if or whether.
  • If the formula is a question (Do you know…?), the sentence takes a question mark; if it is a statement (I'd like to know…), it takes a period.

lecciones.t: Oficios, lugares de trabajo y actividades
lecciones.content_es:
Sectores y cargos

manager, supervisor, assistant, analyst, technician, consultant, intern (practicante), freelancer, entrepreneur (emprendedor), civil servant (funcionario público).

Lugares

office, workshop (taller), warehouse (bodega), factory, site (obra), lab, headquarters (sede central), remote / hybrid work.

Actividades

attend meetings, meet deadlines (cumplir plazos), handle complaints, draft reports, supervise a team, negotiate contracts, track progress, troubleshoot (resolver fallas).

Condiciones

full-time / part-time, shift (turno), salary vs wage (mensual vs por hora), benefits, promotion, resign (renunciar), be laid off (ser despedido por recorte).

lecciones.content_es:
Habilidades duras y blandas

hard skills: data analysis, programming, bilingual proficiency, technical drawing.
soft skills: teamwork, leadership, communication, adaptability, time management, problem-solving, critical thinking.

Cómo describirlas

  • I'm good at solving problems. (good at + gerundio)
  • I have experience in customer service.
  • One of my strengths is attention to detail.
  • I'm able to work under pressure.

Debilidades sin dispararse en el pie

Se menciona la debilidad y de inmediato la acción correctiva: I used to struggle with public speaking, but I've been taking a course and I've improved a lot.

Ojo

Ability es la capacidad; skill es la habilidad entrenada. Career es la trayectoria profesional, no la carrera universitaria (que es degree o major).
lecciones.content_en:
Hard and soft skills

hard skills: data analysis, programming, bilingual proficiency, technical drawing.
soft skills: teamwork, leadership, communication, adaptability, time management, problem-solving, critical thinking.

How to describe them

  • I'm good at solving problems. (good at + gerund)
  • I have experience in customer service.
  • One of my strengths is attention to detail.
  • I'm able to work under pressure.

Weaknesses without shooting yourself in the foot

State the weakness and immediately the corrective action: I used to struggle with public speaking, but I've been taking a course and I've improved a lot.

Careful

Ability is the capacity; skill is the trained competence. Career is your professional path, not a university programme (that is a degree or major).

lecciones.content_es:
Documentos

résumé / CV, cover letter (carta de presentación), reference, portfolio, job posting (oferta de empleo), application.

Preguntas típicas

Tell me about yourself. · Why are you interested in this position? · What are your strengths and weaknesses? · Where do you see yourself in five years? · Can you give an example of a challenge you faced?

Cómo responder

Estructura situación → acción → resultado: In my last project, the deadline moved up. I reorganized the schedule and delegated two tasks. We delivered on time.

Correos de trabajo

Dear Mr. Ospina, · I am writing to apply for… · Please find my résumé attached. · I look forward to hearing from you. · Best regards,

Ojo

Apply for a job, apply to a company. Y attach es adjuntar: Please find attached…
lecciones.content_en:
Documents

résumé / CV, cover letter, reference, portfolio, job posting, application.

Typical questions

Tell me about yourself. · Why are you interested in this position? · What are your strengths and weaknesses? · Where do you see yourself in five years? · Can you give an example of a challenge you faced?

How to answer

Use the situation → action → result structure: In my last project, the deadline moved up. I reorganized the schedule and delegated two tasks. We delivered on time.

Work emails

Dear Mr. Ospina, · I am writing to apply for… · Please find my résumé attached. · I look forward to hearing from you. · Best regards,

Careful

Apply for a job, apply to a company. And attach means to send with the message: Please find attached…

repaso.titulo: Repaso — Professional Communication and Life Skills
repaso.titulo_en: Review — Professional Communication and Life Skills
repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

El registro profesional se construye con modales (para graduar obligación, consejo y cortesía), conjunciones subordinantes (para articular ideas complejas) y preguntas indirectas (para sonar formal y respetuoso).

Puntos gramaticales

  • Los modales no llevan -s ni to; se sustituyen por be able to, have to y be allowed to en otros tiempos.
  • Modal perfecto = modal + have + participio. Nunca would of.
  • so that expresa propósito; so … that y such … that expresan resultado.
  • En preguntas indirectas el orden es el de una afirmación, sin do/does/did.

Vocabulario

Cargos y lugares de trabajo, hard y soft skills, fortalezas y debilidades, documentos y fórmulas de correo profesional.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

Professional register is built with modals (to grade obligation, advice and politeness), subordinating conjunctions (to articulate complex ideas) and indirect questions (to sound formal and respectful).

Grammar points

  • Modals take no -s and no to; they are replaced by be able to, have to and be allowed to in other tenses.
  • Perfect modal = modal + have + participle. Never would of.
  • so that expresses purpose; so … that and such … that express result.
  • In indirect questions the order is that of a statement, with no do/does/did.

Vocabulary

Roles and workplaces, hard and soft skills, strengths and weaknesses, documents and professional email formulas.
